title: Sum the readings
prompt: Return the sum of all numeric readings; an empty array totals zero.
explanation: The accumulator is overwritten on every iteration. Add each reading to keep the running total.

title: Largest value
prompt: Return the largest number in a nonempty array, including arrays of negative numbers.
explanation: Starting from 0 hides negative maxima. Start from the first element instead.

title: Detect odd numbers
prompt: Return true when an integer is odd, including negative integers.
explanation: In JavaScript the remainder keeps the sign of the dividend, so -3 % 2 is -1. Compare against zero instead.

title: Last element
prompt: Return the last element of a nonempty array.
explanation: Array indexes start at zero, so the last valid index is length minus one.

title: Capitalize a word
prompt: Return the word with only its first letter converted to uppercase.
explanation: slice(0) copies the whole word, so the first letter is duplicated. Skip it with slice(1).

title: First negative index
prompt: Return the index of the first negative number, or -1 when there is none.
explanation: The loop starts at index 1 and never inspects the first element.

title: Unique sorted numbers
prompt: Return the distinct numbers in ascending numeric order.
explanation: Without a comparator, sort() compares values as strings, so 10 comes before 9. Pass a numeric comparator.

title: Remove without mutation
prompt: Return a new array without the element at the index and leave the input unchanged.
explanation: Assigning an array copies only the reference, so splice changes the caller's array. Copy it first.

title: Cart total
prompt: Return the total cost of cart items, where each item has price and qty.
explanation: The quantity is ignored, so every item is counted once. Multiply the price by qty.

title: Contains a character
prompt: Return true only when the text contains the character.
explanation: indexOf returns 0 for a match at the start (falsy) and -1 for no match (truthy). Compare with -1 explicitly.

title: Binary search
prompt: Return the index of target in a sorted array, or -1 when it is absent.
explanation: When low equals high one candidate remains. The strict comparison skips it, so the last element can be missed.

title: Closures in a loop
prompt: Return one function per element that later returns that element.
explanation: var is function scoped, so every closure shares one index that ends past the array. let creates a fresh binding per iteration.

title: Balanced parentheses
prompt: Return true when every opening parenthesis has a matching closing one.
explanation: Unclosed opening parentheses remain on the stack. The function must report balance only when the stack is empty.

title: Longest equal run
prompt: Return the length of the longest run of equal neighbouring values.
explanation: A new run already contains one element. Resetting to zero undercounts every run by one.

title: Median
prompt: Return the median of a nonempty array of numbers.
explanation: An even-length array has two middle values. Their average is the median, not just the upper one.

title: Sum positives
prompt: Return the sum of strictly positive values.
explanation: The condition selects negative numbers. It should select values greater than zero.

title: Count lowercase vowels
prompt: Count every lowercase vowel in a string.
explanation: Without the global flag, match returns only the first match with its groups. Add g to collect all matches.

title: Reverse a string
prompt: Return the characters of a string in reverse order.
explanation: Joining with a space inserts separators between letters. Join with an empty string.

title: Palindrome check
prompt: Return true when text reads the same forwards and backwards.
explanation: A string is never strictly equal to an array. Join the reversed characters before comparing.

title: Average
prompt: Return the arithmetic mean of a nonempty array of numbers.
explanation: The divisor is one too small. Divide by the number of values.

title: Clamp a number
prompt: Limit a value to the inclusive range from min to max.
explanation: A value below the range should snap to the lower bound, not the upper one.

title: Repeat text
prompt: Return the text repeated exactly times times.
explanation: With <= the loop runs one extra time. Stop before i reaches times.

title: Double every number
prompt: Return a new array with every number multiplied by two.
explanation: A braced arrow function needs an explicit return. Without it, map produces undefined values.

title: Smallest value
prompt: Return the smallest number in a nonempty array.
explanation: The comparison is reversed, so the loop never replaces Infinity. Use less than.

title: Count even numbers
prompt: Return how many values in the array are even.
explanation: Assigning 1 means the result can never exceed one. Increment the counter instead.

title: Second largest number
prompt: Return the second largest number in an array of at least two numbers.
explanation: The default sort is lexicographic, so 100 sorts before 9. Provide a numeric comparator.

title: Split into chunks
prompt: Split an array into consecutive chunks of the given size.
explanation: slice takes an end index, not a length. After the first chunk the end must move forward with i.

title: Sum of digits
prompt: Return the sum of the decimal digits of a nonnegative integer.
explanation: Division in JavaScript is not integer division. Floor the quotient or the number keeps a fraction.

title: Apply default options
prompt: Return options merged over defaults so caller values win.
explanation: Later spread entries overwrite earlier ones. The caller's options must come last.
tests: assert.deepStrictEqual(withDefaults({ a: 1 }, { a: 2, b: 3 }), { a: 1, b: 3 });

title: Count words
prompt: Count words separated by any amount of whitespace.
explanation: Splitting on one space creates empty entries for repeated spaces. Split on a whitespace pattern.

title: Ascending order check
prompt: Return true when numbers are in nondecreasing order.
explanation: The comparison rejects ascending pairs. A violation is a value smaller than its predecessor.

title: Rotate left
prompt: Rotate an array left by k positions without losing elements.
explanation: The tail concatenation stops one element early, so an element disappears.

title: Own key check
prompt: Return true when an object has the key, even when its value is falsy.
explanation: Checking the value fails for 0, empty strings and false. Test for the key itself.

title: Inclusive range
prompt: Return every integer from start to end, including both ends.
explanation: The strict comparison leaves out the final number. Use <= to include it.

title: Capitalize each word
prompt: Capitalize the first letter of every space separated word.
explanation: Joining with an empty string removes the spaces between words.

title: Fibonacci number
prompt: Return the nth Fibonacci number where fibonacci(0) is 0 and fibonacci(1) is 1.
explanation: After previous is replaced, current is assigned that same value. The new term next is lost.

title: Merge sorted arrays
prompt: Merge two ascending arrays into one ascending array.
explanation: When one side is exhausted the other may still have elements. Append both remainders.

title: First unique character
prompt: Return the first character that appears exactly once, or null.
explanation: The second loop returns the first repeated character. It must return the first one counted once.

title: Two sum
prompt: Return the indexes of two different elements that add up to target, or null.
explanation: The map must remember the values already visited, not the values still needed.

title: Group words by length
prompt: Group words into arrays keyed by their length.
explanation: The group array is replaced by a single word on every iteration. Push the word into the group instead.

title: Sum async values
prompt: Await every asynchronous load and return the total.
explanation: load returns a promise. Without await the promise is added to the number instead of its result.

title: Counter closure
prompt: Return a counter whose value() reads the count without changing it.
explanation: Reading the value also increments it, so every read changes the result. A getter must be free of side effects.
tests: const c = createCounter(); c.increment(); assert.strictEqual(c.value(), 1); assert.strictEqual(c.value(), 1);

title: Remove duplicates
prompt: Remove repeated values but keep the first occurrence of each value in order.
explanation: The predicate drops every value that appears more than once. Keep an element only at its first index.

title: Parse integers
prompt: Convert numeric strings to base 10 integers and drop invalid ones.
explanation: map passes the index as the second argument, which parseInt treats as the radix. Wrap the call and pass 10.

title: Sort people by age
prompt: Return a new array of people sorted by ascending age.
explanation: A comparator must return a negative, zero or positive number. A boolean never signals that a should come first.
tests: assert.deepStrictEqual(sortByAge([{ age: 9 }, { age: 4 }, { age: 7 }, { age: 1 }]).map((p) => p.age), [1, 4, 7, 9]);
